Person: woman in denim jacket, arms crossed resting on the hood/fender just ahead of the driver-side A-pillar, from 00:00 to 00:09.75; no traversal between spaces occurs.

Person position vs openings: her torso rises out of the cowl/fender junction directly in front of the windshield; the near-side fender, door and front wheel below her are fully unoccluded (00:00-00:02.75), and in close views (00:05-00:09.75) the cabin seat is visible directly behind her through the windshield/side glass — she occupies the boundary between interior and exterior where no opening exists.

findings.description: The woman's torso emerges from the cowl/fender area in front of the driver-side windshield edge, arms crossed on the hood. If she were standing outside beside the car, her body and legs would occlude the near-side fender, door and front wheel, but those panels are completely unobstructed below her (clearly at 00:00-00:02.75). In the closer views (00:05-00:09.75) the cabin seat back sits directly behind her through the glass, implying she is inside the cabin yet projecting through the closed windshield/cowl where no opening exists. No position — inside or outside — is consistent with the established car body and its openings; this persists for the whole clip.
